# Baochip-1x peripherals — plain-English guide

This folder turns the official Baochip-1x hardware documentation into a practical reading guide. It is written for someone who understands software but is still learning how chips, pins, clocks and peripherals fit together.

**Primary reference:** [Baochip-1x autogenerated register documentation](https://ci.betrusted.io/bao1x/)

**Source book:** [baochip/baochip-1x — docs](https://github.com/baochip/baochip-1x/tree/main/docs/src)

## Start here

The Baochip is not just a CPU. It also contains hardware blocks that do specific jobs: UART handles serial communication, I²C and SPI connect external chips, ADC measures analog voltages, PWM generates timed output signals, and BIO is a small programmable I/O processor.

A useful mental model:

```text
Your Xous application
       |
       v
A driver / hardware service
       |
       v
A peripheral block inside the Baochip
       |
       v
A pin, another chip, memory, or a signal
```

An application normally asks a driver or Xous service to use hardware. It should not assume it can safely take over a shared peripheral or pin by writing registers itself.

## How to read the register-reference site

The landing page at https://ci.betrusted.io/bao1x/ is an index. It groups the chip's automatically extracted documentation into:
- **Modules:** for example, the interrupt controller.
- **Register groups:** named blocks such as BIO_BDMA, IOX, PWM, UDMA_CTRL, UDMA_I2C_0 and UDMA_I2S.
- **FIFO register groups:** BIO_FIFO0 through BIO_FIFO3.

Each register-group page describes the registers, bit fields, reset values, access types and links toward RTL. Think of it as the hardware's detailed control-panel map, not as a beginner tutorial.

The chip project's own book says the automatic register extraction covers about 98% of chip functions. It also says that a number of driver-level subjects (including UDMA UART, SPIM, I2C, SDIO and camera) are potential topics for future supplemental documentation. That means a register map may exist even when the book does not yet explain the complete software bring-up sequence.

## Important distinction: a peripheral block is not the same as a board connector

The Baochip has peripheral logic inside the chip. The Dabao board exposes only selected chip pins at its headers. Before connecting a component, check all three:
1. The component's electrical interface and voltage requirements.
2. The Baochip pinout and alternate-function mapping.
3. The board schematic/header mapping for the particular Dabao revision.

A register-map page cannot tell you, by itself, which header hole you should wire to.

## Documentation boundaries

These files are plain-English explanations of the linked official documentation. Where the source book is detailed, the notes explain its actual details. Where only a register-group name or index entry is available, the notes say so rather than inventing programming behaviour.

The generated register pages are the authority for exact register fields. Confirm details against the live page and the RTL for the silicon stepping you are using before writing low-level code.
